To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
melanocortins are effective in the treatment of peripheral nerve diseases.

the peptide melanocytostatic hormone (MSH) and its precursor, adrenocorticotropin (ACTH), are effective in promoting regeneration and recovery of function following experimental peripheral nerve trauma, and that the melanocortin receptor antagonist, SHU-9119, is effective in preventing regeneration and recovery following nerve trauma.
melanocortins are neuroprotective and neurorestorative in peripheral nerves, and that they are effective in the treatment of experimental neuropathies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the neurotrophic and pharmacotherapeutic potential of the melanocortin peptides in the peripheral nervous system.
the development and evaluation of new pharmacotherapeutic agents for the treatment of peripheral nerve diseases.
the development of new leads in peripheral nervous system pharmacotherapy, and we are particularly interested in the potential of melanotropins in this field.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the melanocortin peptides have the potential to be effective pharmacotherapeutics in a wide range of nervous system disorders, including those of the central and peripheral nervous system.
the use of melanotropins and their analogs in experimental neurology and neuropharmacology has led to a new and promising avenue in the treatment of nerve disorders.

the use of animal models of peripheral nerve disease, in combination with the use of melanocortins, is an important tool to study the pathophysiology of peripheral nerve disorders and may be of great value in the search for new leads for pharmacotherapeutic intervention in these diseases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of melanotropins in peripheral nerve injury and disease may be based on the following considerations: (a) the presence of MSH receptors in the central and peripheral nervous systems, and their potential involvement in neuronal survival; (b) the neurotrophic activity of MSH in tissue culture; (c) the beneficial effects of ACTH and MSH in peripheral nerve injury in animals; and (d) the beneficial effects on human peripheral nerve disorders.

melanocortins and gangliosides are effective in enhancing the functional and structural recovery of peripheral nerves following traumatic injury, and also in protection or repair of the nerve following intoxication.
melanocortins are neuroprotective in peripheral neuropathy, and that the neuroprotective effects are mediated by the melanocortin receptors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of animal models of nerve injury, intoxication, or degenerative diseases is a valid approach to screen potential neuroprotective compounds.
the melanocortin system is a new lead in the development of pharmacotherapeutics that may be useful in the treatment of peripheral nerve disorders.
the use of melanocortins in peripheral neuropathies is promising and that further studies are required to elucidate the molecular mechanism(s) underlying the therapeutic effect of these peptides.
